terms: ## Conversational Texture The operator asked to cross-review B-12d7 with genuine two hosts after Codex caught a real ordering bug in B-7691 that degraded Claude-only review had missed. Codex (host 2) then found these two B-12d7 bugs -- the same pattern. This fix is driven with genuine Claude + Codex 2-host review (Codex as a real second provider-host, not the unreachable Authority server, and not a fabricated single host).

## Key Insights Both were MASKED by the B-12d7 smoke: it asserted a transcript key only at the envelope TOP LEVEL (not inside the usage object), and it asserted recordDispatchFinalForProvider 'never throws' for prompt_tokens:-999 but NOT that an unavailable final is still written. The claude/anthropic path (recordDispatchFinal) has the same swallow-on-throw shape but is out of scope here (byte-identical). Fix: (1) project the extractor output to ONLY the known token-count fields -- openai: prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/prompt_tokens_details; gemini: promptTokenCount/candidatesTokenCount/cachedContentTokenCount -- dropping any other key; (2) in recordDispatchFinalForProvider, wrap the buildProviderRecord+append in an inner try so a throw falls through to the unavailable-final branch (estimate still superseded), preserving the never-throws fail-open guarantee.

## Solution Tradeoffs Token-only projection is defense-in-depth (real OpenAI/Gemini usage objects carry only token counts, but the invariant must be ENFORCED not assumed). The unavailable-on-throw fix keeps ledger accounting consistent (the estimate is always superseded, never orphaned). Keep recordDispatchFinal (anthropic) byte-identical; keep providers/ free of usage-ledger imports; keep the zero-cross-module-import invariant. Extend the smoke to cover both (a non-token key inside usage is dropped; a malformed-object usage writes an unavailable final that supersedes the estimate).

## Trigger Event On 2026-06-19 a genuine Codex CLI host-2 cross-review (codex exec) of merged story B-12d7 returned VERDICT: FAIL with two HIGH findings, both verified against the real code: (1) extractCodexUsage (packages/main/src/providers/codex-cli.ts ~line 101) and extractGeminiUsage (gemini-cli.ts ~line 104) return the whole provider `usage`/`usageMetadata` sub-object verbatim; a non-token key embedded inside it survives into ProviderExecResult.reportedUsage, contradicting the JSDoc's 'returns ONLY the numeric usage sub-object, NEVER transcript text'. (2) recordDispatchFinalForProvider (core/usage-ledger/dispatch-usage.ts ~line 427): a usable-but-malformed usage object (e.g. prompt_tokens:-999) makes buildProviderRecord throw; the function's outer try/catch swallows it and SKIPS the unavailable-final branch below, so no final record is written and the preflight estimate is never superseded.

A genuine Codex host-2 cross-review of merged story B-12d7 (VERDICT: FAIL) found two real correctness gaps the Claude-only review missed. (1) extractCodexUsage/extractGeminiUsage return the WHOLE provider usage sub-object verbatim, so a non-token key embedded inside `usage` (e.g. a transcript field) would survive into ProviderExecResult.reportedUsage, contradicting the 'numeric token fields only, never raw transcript' invariant the JSDoc claims. (2) recordDispatchFinalForProvider: when a usable-but-malformed usage object (e.g. prompt_tokens:-999) makes buildProviderRecord throw, the outer try/catch swallows it and the unavailable-final branch is skipped, so NO final is written and the preflight estimate is never superseded (orphaned) -- contradicting the design intent that garbage usage still writes an unavailable final that supersedes. This story hardens both, keeping the claude/anthropic path byte-identical, and extends the smoke to cover the cases that masked them.

Harden codex/gemini usage capture: token-only projection + unavailable-final on malformed usage

In packages/main/src/core/usage-ledger/dispatch-usage.ts recordDispatchFinalForProvider: when reportedUsage is a usable object but buildProviderRecord throws (e.g. a malformed/negative token count fails validation), fall through to the unavailable-final branch instead of letting the outer catch swallow everything -- so the preflight estimate is STILL superseded. Wrap the buildProviderRecord + appendUsageRecord in an inner try/catch; on throw, append buildUnavailableFinalRecord (same supersede). Preserve the overall never-throws fail-open guarantee. Do NOT touch recordDispatchFinal (anthropic), parseClaudeCliOutput, the adapters, or buildProviderRecord.

In packages/main/src/providers/codex-cli.ts extractCodexUsage and packages/main/src/providers/gemini-cli.ts extractGeminiUsage: instead of returning the whole matched `usage`/`usageMetadata` object verbatim, return a NEW object containing ONLY the known token-count keys present -- openai: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, prompt_tokens_details; gemini: promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, cachedContentTokenCount (preserve cachedContentTokenCount/prompt_tokens_details as-is for the adapter; drop ANY other key incl. an embedded transcript/text/message). Keep returning undefined when no usage object is present, and keep never-throws. This enforces the raw-output-never-surfaced invariant the JSDoc already claims. Do NOT change ProviderExecResult digest/byte fields or import usage-ledger into providers/.

In packages/main/src/tasks/usage-ledger-codex-gemini-smoke.ts add: (a) extractCodexUsage/extractGeminiUsage given a usage object containing an extra non-token key (e.g. transcript) -> reportedUsage contains ONLY numeric token fields (the extra key is absent); (b) recordDispatchFinalForProvider with a malformed-but-object usage (prompt_tokens:-999) -> an unavailable final IS written AND supersedes the estimate (readLedger shows the unavailable final; summary.estimateCount===0). Keep all existing checks green.
Project extractCodexUsage/extractGeminiUsage output to token-count fields only
recordDispatchFinalForProvider: write an unavailable-final when buildProviderRecord throws
